## Vinyl Liners
Source: https://www.us1pools.com/liners.html

Liners
Fresh patterns, perfect fit.
A new vinyl liner transforms the look and feel of a liner pool. US-1 Pools carries GLI Pool Products, Latham, and Cardinal liners with patterns for in-ground and above-ground replacements.

GLI Pool Products
Latham Pools
Cardinal







GLI Pool Products
Precision-fit vinyl liners.
GLI manufactures custom-measured vinyl liners for both above-ground and in-ground pools. Their liners are made in the USA with virgin vinyl and UV-protected inks for long-lasting color.


Above-ground liners
Overlap, beaded, and unibead styles in 20-mil and 25-mil thickness. Dozens of patterns available.


In-ground liners
Custom-measured to your pool dimensions. 20-mil standard or 28-mil heavy-duty with wall foam backing.


Safety covers
GLI also makes mesh and solid safety covers for winter protection — custom-fit to any pool shape.





Vinyl liner replacement in progress







Latham Pool Products
Latham vinyl liner pattern options.
Latham offers vinyl liner patterns across classic tile-border looks and modern full-print designs. We keep this page focused on liner replacement, not fiberglass shell builds.


Pattern collections
Hundreds of designs from natural stone and mosaic tile to solid colors and geometric prints.


StruXure vinyl
Latham's premium liner material with enhanced durability and stain resistance for lasting performance.





Finished vinyl liner pool







Cardinal Systems
Vinyl liners, steps, and wall systems.
Cardinal manufactures liner-focused pool systems, including vinyl liners, steps, and wall components. We use Cardinal language only for liner and wall-system work, not fiberglass shells.

Cardinal
Latham
GLI

## Pool Care Guide
Source: https://www.us1pools.com/guides/pool-care.html

Resource Center
Pool Care & Maintenance Guide
Everything you need to know to keep your pool crystal clear and equipment running smoothly.






Weekly Maintenance Checklist

Test water chemistry — pH, chlorine, alkalinity (use test strips or bring a sample to our retail counter)
Skim debris — leaves, bugs, and surface contaminants
Brush walls and floor — prevent algae buildup
Vacuum — manual or automatic cleaner
Check filter pressure — backwash if needed
Inspect equipment — listen for unusual pump noise, check for leaks


Water Chemistry Basics

Ideal Ranges for NC Pools:

pH: 7.2 - 7.6
Free Chlorine: 1.0 - 3.0 ppm
Total Alkalinity: 80 - 120 ppm
Calcium Hardness: 200 - 400 ppm
Cyanuric Acid (stabilizer): 30 - 50 ppm

Bring water samples to our Franklinton location for free testing and personalized chemical recommendations.


Winterizing Your Pool (North Carolina)
Most local pools close mid-November through early March. Here's how to winterize properly:

Balance water chemistry one final time before closing.
Lower water level below skimmer and returns (in-ground pools).
Drain and blow out plumbing lines to prevent freeze damage.
Add winterizing chemicals (algaecide and shock).
Cover the pool with a secure winter cover to block debris and sunlight.
Store accessories — ladders, cleaners, and hoses indoors.

Not comfortable doing it yourself? We offer full winterization services — call (919) 441-0033 to schedule.

Opening Your Pool in Spring

Remove and clean your winter cover.
Refill to normal operating level.
Reconnect and inspect all equipment (pumps, filters, heaters).
Shock the pool and run the filter for 24-48 hours.
Test and balance chemistry.
Vacuum debris and brush surfaces.

Want a hassle-free opening? Book our spring startup service and we'll handle everything.

Common Pool Problems & Fixes

Cloudy Water
Causes: High pH, low chlorine, poor filtration, or algae bloom.
Fix: Test and balance chemistry, shock if needed, run filter continuously for 24 hours, and vacuum.


Green Water (Algae)
Causes: Low chlorine or sanitizer failure.
Fix: Brush walls thoroughly, shock heavily (triple dose), run filter 24/7, vacuum to waste (if possible), add algaecide.


Low Pressure at Returns
Causes: Clogged filter, blocked skimmer basket, or air leak in pump.
Fix: Clean or backwash filter, empty skimmer and pump baskets, check for leaks.


When to Call a Pro

Persistent chemical imbalances you can't fix
Pump, filter, or heater malfunctions
Leaks in plumbing or pool structure
Major algae outbreaks
Equipment upgrades or replacements

US-1 Pools offers on-site service, repairs, and equipment installs. Call us at (919) 441-0033 or request service online .





Need Supplies or Expert Advice?
Visit our retail counter in Franklinton for chemicals, test kits, parts, and free water testing.


Get Directions
